title: Meet Iris: England's new two-legged delivery robot
source_used: VTV (Vietnam), via vietnam.vn; Reuters video page returned HTTP 401
key_facts: A two-legged (bipedal) robot named Iris is being tested for parcel delivery in northern England.
It can carry packages of up to 15 kg and moves at up to 6 km an hour.
It can handle stairs and rough ground.
The design is meant for places four-legged robots struggle with, such as narrow alleys and sharp corners.
VTV says this is the first time such a robot has been tested for delivery in Europe.
The developers say Iris is meant to help delivery workers on hard routes, not replace them entirely.
Reuters published a video report titled 'Meet Iris: England's new two-legged delivery robot' on 8 Oct 2026; the text of that video was not available.
quote_evidence: The bipedal robot Iris is currently being tested for deliveries in northern England.
It can carry packages weighing up to 15 kg and moves at a maximum speed of 6 km/hour.
The developers expect the Iris robot to assist delivery workers, handling difficult routes, rather than completely replacing humans.
why_it_matters_hint: A walking robot could reach doorsteps up stairs or down alleys that wheeled and four-legged delivery robots cannot, but this is a trial.
notes: Reuters video page blocked (HTTP 401). Facts come from a short VTV item republished on vietnam.vn, which does not name the developer, the town or the delivery partner; none is invented here. The 'first in Europe' claim is VTV's, not checked independently.
